comments.story: Show HN: An open-source financial ledger API written in Clojure
comments.why: Shows how good table design gives relational-style modeling on NoSQL.
comments.text: I wrote a piece that touches a bit on the why: [LINK] But in a nutshell: availability and scalability. Yes you can achieve this with relational DBs, but it will be quite complex, while No-SQL gives it by design. All while ensuring all the goodness of relational data modeling, consistency and queries. The only requirement is a good table design: [VIDEO]

comments.why: Explains modeling relations in DynamoDB tables.
comments.text: Interesting question. No-SQL doesn't mean non-relational. DynamoDB is a relational database. It's up to you on how you design the table to accommodate your relations. This is a great presentation about this: [VIDEO]
